daily_brief: Trade tensions between the United States and Canada escalated sharply on Saturday after last-minute negotiations collapsed, triggering 50% US tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods and immediate retaliatory measures from Ottawa [BBC, France 24, Globe and Mail]. Prime Minister Mark Carney cited 'unfair, uneconomic' last-minute changes by Washington, while US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer blamed Canadian walkbacks for the breakdown. Meanwhile, Russia continued its assault on Ukraine, with strikes killing at least two people a day after a 'double-tap' drone attack on a shopping center in Kryvyi Rih left 16 dead and over 130 wounded [BBC, France 24]. The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now surpassed 2,500 deaths and is spreading 'exponentially,' with the UN warning the virus is killing one person every 30 minutes [Guardian, RFI, The Hindu]. In the occupied West Bank, Israel re-established the settlement of Kadim, defying international condemnation from France, Germany, Italy, and the UK, who urged immediate withdrawal of new settlement tenders [BBC, France 24, RFI]. US-Iran tensions remain elevated ahead of Monday's announcement of new sanctions, with Tehran vowing a 'devastating' response [Globe and Mail, The Hindu].

top_stories.headline: US-Canada Trade Talks Collapse as 50% Tariffs Take Effect, Ottawa Vows Dollar-for-Dollar Retaliation
bullets: 50% US tariffs on approximately $20 billion of Canadian exports took effect Saturday after negotiations broke down minutes before the deadline
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended talks, citing 'unfair, uneconomic' last-minute changes by US negotiators and questioning 'the reliability of any deal'
Canada announced it will impose reciprocal tariffs on US goods 'dollar for dollar' to protect Canadian workers and businesses
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada 'declined to finalize the trade deal under the terms agreed earlier this week' despite offers of tariff reductions in steel and aluminum

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Carney's statement about unreliable US negotiating terms

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Highlighted Trump's earlier optimism about reaching a deal

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Provided broader context on Trump's trade policy record and its limited success delivering promised economic benefits

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Focused on factual breakdown of tariff timeline

top_stories.headline: Russian Double-Tap Strike Kills 16 at Ukrainian Shopping Center, Strikes Continue Saturday
bullets: A daytime Russian drone attack on a busy shopping center in Kryvyi Rih killed 16 people and injured over 130, including 23 children, with 9 still missing
President Zelensky called the attack 'absolutely cynical and despicable,' stating a second drone struck 30 minutes after the first, targeting emergency responders
Additional Russian strikes Saturday killed at least two more people—one in a Kyiv warehouse fire from a ballistic missile, another in a drone strike on Zaporizhzhia
Russia's defense ministry said it launched massive strikes targeting transport infrastructure and warehouses; it has not commented on the shopping center attack

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Included verified BBC footage of the second drone strike

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Zelensky's characterization of the attack as terrorism

top_stories.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Now Deadliest in Country's History, Growing 'Exponentially'
bullets: More than 2,500 people have died in the DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, surpassing the 2018-20 outbreak's toll, with half the deaths occurring in the last 20 days
The outbreak is spreading faster than any Ebola outbreak in recorded history, now affecting six provinces across an area larger than France
Over 16,000 doses of Ervebo vaccine arrived Friday, though the vaccine is approved for the Zaire strain, not the circulating Bundibugyo strain—its effectiveness against this strain remains unproven
The UN warned Ebola is killing one person every 30 minutes in DRC; WHO says the outbreak is on track to surpass the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic as the largest ever

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized historical comparison and speed of spread

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Featured MSF warnings about response capacity being outpaced

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Criticized Canada's comparatively small aid contribution

top_stories.headline: Israel Re-Establishes Closed West Bank Settlement as European Allies Issue Joint Condemnation
bullets: Thirty Israeli settler families moved into the settlement of Kadim near Jenin, reopening it 20 years after it was closed by a previous Israeli government
Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich attended the opening ceremony, calling it 'the correction' of an 'expulsion crime'
France, Germany, Italy, and the UK issued a joint statement calling on Israel to halt settlement expansion and withdraw tenders for over 1,200 new homes under the E1 project
Israeli settlers separately shot and killed a 17-year-old Palestinian boy near Hebron on Friday; UN called for accountability as 22 Palestinians have been killed in settler attacks this year

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Noted all Israeli settlements are illegal under international law

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Detailed the separate shooting death of the Palestinian teenager

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Emphasized European diplomatic pressure and two-state solution concerns

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Highlighted UN response and broader pattern of settler violence

top_stories.headline: US-Iran Tensions Intensify Ahead of 'Toughest Sanctions in History' Announcement
bullets: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will announce new sanctions on Iran Monday, described by administration officials as 'the toughest sanctions in history'
Iran's Foreign Ministry called secondary sanctions an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty' with no foundation in international law and vowed a 'devastating' response
Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have virtually halted as Iran threatens to strike unauthorized tankers; China, which buys over 80% of Iran's shipped oil, urged diplomacy
President Trump said Iran 'would love to make a deal' but is 'not ready to make the right deal,' reiterating the US will not allow Iran to obtain nuclear weapons

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed context on China's role and strategic oil dynamics

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Trump's rally remarks and nuclear weapons focus
